newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Ethnic Albanian loyalist killed in Kosovo.
newsitem.headline: Ethnic Albanian loyalist killed in Kosovo.

text.p: An ethnic Albanian loyal to Serb authorities in Belgrade was shot in Podujevo, a town in Serbia's southern troubled province of Kosovo, local media reported on Friday.
Maliq Sheholi, a member of the ruling Serbian Socialist Party (SPS) of President Slobodan Milosevic, was killed on Thursday afternoon in the centre of the town, Radio Prishtina reported.
The radio quoted witnesses as saying unidentified assailants fired three bullets at Sheholi, two of which hit him.
Shelholi died on his way to hospital.
No organisation has claimed responsibility for the killing.

An ethnic Albanian organisation, the Kosovo Liberation Army, said after it claimed the killing of two Serbs last October in Podujevo, that it "would soon knock at the door of Albanians cooperating with the Serb occupier."
Several Serbian police have been killed since the beginning of last year. Ninety per cent of Kosovo's population are ethnic Albanians.
Belgrade stripped the province of its autonomy in 1989, saying the Albanians wanted to secede from Serbia.
Since then, most Albanians have rejected Serbian authority accusing Serbia of systematic human rights abuses.
